name: sort
algorithm: Each standard library's unstable sort of n u64 values: per round r the values are splitmix64 from seed + r * 0x5555555555555555, sorted ascending, and every 1,024th value times its index plus the last value is added to the checksum with wrapping (README.md).

skip.mk-wrap: the checksum already uses the wrapping operators; there is no checked arithmetic to remove

no_counts: B24 does not apply: an idiomatic row compares libraries, each with its own algorithm; the sorted order of distinct keys is unique, so the sampled checksum checks every column sorted
notes: Algorithms: Mk Slice.Sort is Go's pdqsort_func (plan/19-std.md S-7) with the comparator inlined; Rust slice::sort_unstable is ipnsort; Zig std.mem.sortUnstable is pdqsort; Go slices.Sort is pdqsort; C qsort is the C runtime's (UCRT on Windows), with an indirect comparison call per compare.
